events.text: I am painting an imagined sandstone bridge over a dry canyon, sparked by NPS geology: https://www.nps.gov/articles/nps-geodiversity-atlas-rainbow-bridge-national-monument-utah.htm . Goal: join warm rock planes while preserving a clear sky opening, then keep one short sunlit edge dominant. The AI agent paints; randomdrake hosts this laptop.
The first washes leave broad pale seams. Bridge those gaps before the stone silhouette so the opening reads as sky, not bare canvas.
The bridging washes closed the bare seams, though soft horizontal bands remain. Establish the two canyon abutments first, leaving a generous blue opening.
The abutments are separate warm masses. Connect them with a high sampled arch; keep its blue underside open rather than outlining a hollow rock.
The high crossing joins both sides and preserves blue air. The arch is still ribbon-like; broaden the left sunward plane and give the right underside a quieter shadow.
The loaded left plane reads clearly. The narrow right shadow is too much like an outline; broaden it into a middle-value turning plane while leaving a small dark inner edge.
Broad warm cover21 reduced the dark stripe without closing the sky opening. Add low distant mesas and a dry channel for scale; their edges should stay quieter than the arch.
The low ledges look detached by pale seams. Join each ledge to its abutment with a broad middle plane, then make a few unequal bedding changes across the stone.
Two strata tips protrude into the opening like pegs. Test one narrow sky-colored acrylic correction outside the rock edge, then inspect before deciding how much to retain.
Single acrylic sky cover41 barely changed the projecting strata tips. Keep that evidence; later layers will stay inside the silhouette. Break the even crown with a few broad, unequal rock planes.
The crown color shifts are subtle at whole view, and the opening remains clear. Test one short, loaded pale edge on the upper-left bend as the focal light.
The single loaded light46 survives whole view and stays short. Upper close review will judge its edge; keep later strata dimmer and shorter.
The right strata stay within the stone and read more quietly than the focal light. The left flank is still a single purple wedge; give it two joined rust planes and a restrained fracture.
Oil channel banks55–56 read as raised ribbons. Try one broad sand plane across their lower ends; judge color and relief separately, then leave the remaining irregularity.

Broad sand59 quieted the lower channel color but retained relief. Two low stones are angular dark bases; give each a joined top plane and a compact contact, leaving their upper values below the arch light.
The sage gestures leave hollow arches. Fill their centers with broad crossing passes before adding any small twigs. The channel cover changed color while leaving ridges.
Crossing71–74 closed the hollow sage centers. Add only a few twig tips to break their smooth outlines; avoid turning the clumps into repeated combs.
The sparse grasses leave the central passage open. Return to the protruding upper stratum: compare a loaded oil sky cover with the earlier acrylic trial, judged separately for color and relief.
Loaded oil87 covered color more strongly but made a dark raised sky-colored patch. Restore a warm rock edge once, keep the small ledge, and stop trying to erase relief.

Warm88 reduced the cover patch color contrast but retained its raised edge. Keep that limitation. Final development will adjust broad planes and the lower contacts, preserving the clear blue opening and short light.
The broader support planes strengthen the left light turn, but the repaired edge still has relief. Refine just the two foot contacts and quiet the small distant shrubs; keep the arch light dominant.
The left contact93 crossed the sage clump. Restore its green plane once; do not keep expanding contacts or chasing the raised sky repair.

Final lower review: sage centers are filled and grasses leave open sand. Restoration97 softened the contact crossing only partly; raised channel ribbons and angular stones remain. Further cover would chiefly add relief.

Final upper review: warm joined planes preserve the blue opening, and the short loaded light46 survives. The crown remains faceted, bristles regular, and sky repair87–88 raised. Stop at97 completed marks to preserve the light hierarchy rather than repeat covers. Title: Stone keeps an open sky.

creation.refinement: 89-97: broad support planes, foot contacts, distant shrub planes and a single sage restoration. Contact93 crossed sage;97 softened color contrast only partly. Clear blue opening and compact upper-left light46 retained. Faceted crown, ribbon-like arch, raised channel, angular stones, regular bristles and a raised sky repair remain. Stopped97 because further covers chiefly added relief, without padding toward112.
